name: SuperX
tagline: AI content, smart scheduling, engagement tools, and analytics for growing on X

pricing.notes: Pro at $49/month (5 accounts, 500 posts, AI credits, auto DMs); Advanced at $49 launch price (normally $99); Ultra $199.
pricing.freeTier: No free plan, only a time-limited trial before picking a paid tier.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 5 X accounts, 500 posts/month, 500 AI credits/month, 1 Signal Agent with 750 leads/day, 1,000 automated DMs/month and 10 cover images/month.

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.limits: 750 posts/month, 1,000 AI credits/month, 750 Engage replies/month, 3 Signal Agents with 3,000 leads/day, 1,000 DMs/month, 20 covers/month and 120 API requests/minute.
tiers.notes: Live launch price is $49/month and the page also displays $99 as the normal price; no dated price-change record was available.

tiers.name: Ultra
tiers.limits: 10 X accounts, 3,000 posts/month, 4,000 AI credits/month, 3,000 replies/month, 5 agents with 7,500 leads/day, 5,000 DMs/month and 400 API requests/minute.
tiers.notes: AI credits can be expanded to 100,000, but the add-on price is not public.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; the live page offers a time-limited trial but does not publish its numeric duration
pricing.billingTerms: monthly only, no annual plan shown; refunds considered case-by-case within 7 days
pricing.hiddenCosts: X Articles consume 2 post credits and require a separate X Premium subscription for every connected account. Increasing Ultra from 4,000 to as many as 100,000 AI credits may cost extra, but no rate is public.

verdictSummary: The personal core (a composer with an LLM writing in your voice, a slot-based scheduler, and basic analytics) is a weekend build, exactly like every scheduler on this list. What you cannot one-shot: X's write API costs real money before your first post goes out, the 10M-post viral library and timing models are proprietary data collected over years, and the engagement automations live in rate-limit and ToS territory that a personal script will get wrong. Full disclosure: SuperX is built by the person who runs this site. The verdict got no mercy anyway.
coreLoopDIY: Compose posts and threads with an LLM prompted on samples of your own writing, queue them into weekday time slots, publish via the X API, and pull your post metrics into a local dashboard.
requirements: paid X API tier for posting
LLM API key for voice-matched drafts
whatYouLose: the 10M+ viral post library and niche inspiration feed
whyPeopleStillPay: The X API meters every write before your first post, so the DIY version starts at a monthly API bill with none of the product. The parts that grow an account (knowing what performs in your niche, when to post it, and which conversations are worth joining) come from data SuperX has been collecting and modelling for years, not from code you can regenerate.

notes: The site owner's own product. Listed at community request, judged by the same rubric as everything else.
prompt:
Build me a personal X posting cockpit inspired by SuperX. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3, one localhost web app; no accounts, no
  telemetry, all keys in .env.
- A composer with an AI draft panel: send my topic plus 20 of my own past
  posts (pasted once into voice.txt) to an LLM API so drafts sound like me,
  with tone buttons for punchier, shorter, thread.
- Slot-based queue: weekday posting times in my timezone from a config
  file; drafts fill the next free slot, drag to reorder, pin to exact
  datetimes. Thread support with per-post character counters.
- Publish via the X API v2 with node-cron, marking rows sent or failed
  before posting so nothing double-posts. Be blunt in the README: posting
  needs a paid X API tier, and that bill exists before the first post.
- Pull my recent post metrics (impressions, likes, replies) on a daily
  cron into SQLite and render a simple dashboard: per-post table plus a
  30-day sparkline drawn as inline SVG.
- A fallback copy-to-clipboard button per queued post so the tool stays
  useful without paying X anything.
- Out of scope, and say so in the README: viral post libraries, optimal
  timing models, auto-DMs, lead generation, and multi-account. Those are
  data and ToS problems, not code.
- README: X developer app setup, which paid tier posting needs, and the
  LLM key.
